subject: Copy order and quotation: SE/RA/25.3/4/II/7/B, document (b), and SE/RA/721512/II/II 1/II 1 B/4
body:
Dear Riksarkivet,

I write on behalf of a small non-commercial project that reads cipher passages in historical letters and documents. One person directs the project and sends every message; the searches of the printed editions, the reading of images and the audits are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in a public repository, where every step is logged. I say this at the outset so you know whom you are dealing with.

I would like to order digital copies (scans, 400 dpi or whatever your standard photographic quality is) of two items, and would be grateful for a quotation before any work is done.

1. Reference code SE/RA/25.3/4/II/7/B (Originaltraktater med främmande makter / Tyskland / Kejsaren (Österrike-Ungern) / Fredsfördrag med tillägg). Your catalogue lists two documents under this code; I ask only for document (b): "Konung Karl XI:s fullmakt för svenske kommissarierna, Nääs, 6 maj 1677. Latin, delvis i chiffer. Papper, 3 sidor text, sigill." -- all three pages of text, and the seal side if it carries any writing. Document (a), Stockholm 12 April 1676, is not needed.

The reason: the catalogue describes document (b) as partly in cipher, and we have not found its cipher passage printed or deciphered anywhere. We checked that Sverges traktater med främmande magter has no part covering 1648-1723 (LIBRIS lists the series running from D. 6, 1646-1648, to D. 8, 1723-1771), searched the full text of 28 scans of the printed Nijmegen congress papers (Actes et mémoires in French and German, the 1678 Recueil, St Disdier and Dumont's Corps universel diplomatique) for the Nääs full power without finding it (a search of OCR text; it is a test only for the 19 scans in which a control term such as Oxenstierna, Suède or Nimègue was found, not for the other 9), and read the Swedish full power printed in the German Nimwegisch Friedens-Memorial of 1680 (pp. 102-104): it is dated at Stockholm ("Castel Holm"), 12 April 1676, the date and place of your document (a), not the 1677 one. The record also shows the document is not digitised. If (b) follows the formulary of (a), the printed 1676 text (a German translation) may help read its plain-Latin parts, and so where the cipher passage sits; the full record of these checks is at the "item 1" link below.

2. Reference code SE/RA/721512/II/II 1/II 1 B/4 (Beskickningsarkivet från Biby / Beskickningarna till Konstantinopel 1737-1779 / Korrespondens / Korrespondens med hemlandet). Your catalogue describes it as: "Brevkoncept av Gustaf Celsing till Georg Wilhelm af Sillén 1755-1757, 1760-1764, odat. Med ett brevkoncept av Gustaf Celsing till greve Ekeblad 3 maj 1763 samt ett odaterat till Nensén. Med chiffernyckel." The record shows it is not digitised, and we do not know how many leaves it has. I would ask first for the cipher key ("chiffernyckel") and any draft written partly in cipher; if it is simpler to scan the whole volume, I would be grateful for the number of leaves and a quotation for that instead.

The reason: the key is filed with the drafts, and we have found no printed text, key or decipherment of this correspondence. We searched the Internet Archive's full-text index and Google Books for Celsing, Sillén and the cipher key, covering scans of Historisk tidskrift, Meddelanden från Svenska Riksarkivet and other Swedish publications (a search that does find other printed Celsing material, so it can see the name), and read Th. Westrin's inventory of Diplomatica Turcica (Meddelanden III, 1891, pp. 411-416), which lists letters from Sillén among Celsing's dispatches but does not name this volume. These are search results, not proof that nothing is in print; the full record is at the "item 2" link below.

If a scan is not possible and either item must be consulted in the reading room, I would be grateful to know. Anything we read from the copies will be published in the repository with a citation of Riksarkivet and the reference codes, and sent to you if it is of interest.

Thank you for your help.
